mainEntity.name: What is a guest home and how is it different from an accessory dwelling unit (ADU)?

acceptedAnswer.text: A guest home, often referred to as an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU), is a secondary residential structure on the same property as a primary single-family home. While 'guest home' might imply a temporary living space, in construction terms, it generally refers to a fully independent living unit. ADUs include a kitchen, bathroom, and sleeping area, functioning as a complete home. They offer benefits like housing for family members, rental income, or a dedicated workspace, and are built to code just like primary residences.
acceptedAnswer.description: A guest home is typically an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU), a complete secondary living space on a single-family property, distinct from the primary home but built to the same codes.
